A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

JIV estimators are consistent, asymptotically normal and have standard errors that are consistent, even when the number of instruments Kn is large and/or grows faster than the number of observations n.
, under the many weak instrument asymptotics, the limiting distributions of JIV estimators are the same as in the homoskedastic case.
JIV estimators are robust to many weak instruments and heteroskedastic IV errors.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the JIV estimator can be a viable alternative to classical IV estimators in many heteroskedastic IV regression models with a large number of weakly identifying instruments.
J IV estimator standard errors can be used to test the null hypothesis of homoskedasticity against the alternative of heteroskedasiticity in a heteroskedastic IV model with many instruments.
